# Counterfact

> Build the frontend. Don’t wait for the backend.

Counterfact turns an OpenAPI document into a useful local API in one command.
Start with a spec, point the frontend at `http://localhost:3100`, and use
schema-derived responses before adding custom handlers. Requires Node.js 22 or
newer. Supports Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1, and 3.2.

```sh
npx counterfact@latest https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json api
```

## Start here

- `docs/getting-started.md` — prerequisite, command, localhost browser request, generated files, and one optional custom response.
- `docs/first-10-minutes.md` — a small create/read workflow and a frontend-relevant failure.
- `docs/usage.md` — task groups for frontend work, team/test work, advanced control, and reference/troubleshooting.

## Use the smallest relevant guide

- `docs/features/routes.md` — custom response handlers.
- `docs/features/state.md` — small shared in-memory state.
- `docs/patterns/simulate-failures.md` and `docs/patterns/simulate-latency.md` — deterministic frontend states.
- `docs/features/proxy.md` — selected upstream paths behind one local base URL.
- `docs/patterns/automated-integration-tests.md` — real HTTP test lifecycle.
- `docs/features/repl.md` — inspect or steer a running local API.
- `docs/reference.md` — CLI flags, `$` API, response builders, and programmatic API.
- `docs/features/without-openapi.md` — alternative path only when no OpenAPI document exists.

Generated `types/` are the endpoint-specific contract. Do not edit them. Edit
handlers in `routes/`, preserve user-authored handler bodies on regeneration,
and run the project’s TypeScript check to find contract drift.
